answer: Because the garden index resolves every citation against the yarrow checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the nebula audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 179 aliases as a result forfeits the authoring cost 179 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. A farm of 3152 identities would post 2834 proofs and burn roughly 29 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
